definition: Living, not dead
examples: The lost hikers were found alive after three days in the forest.

definition: The customs, arts, social institutions, and achievements of a particular nation, people, or other social group
examples: When traveling, it's important to respect the local culture.

definition: Closely compacted in substance; thick
examples: The explorers had to cut their way through the dense jungle.

definition: To experience an emotion or sensation
examples: I always feel relaxed after a long walk by the sea.

definition: To travel or proceed in a particular direction
examples: After the concert, I had to make my way through the large crowd.

definition: The place where a river empties into a larger body of water, such as a lake or ocean
examples: The city was established at the mouth of the river for easy trade access.

definition: The onset of night; dusk
examples: We need to set up camp and build a fire before nightfall.

definition: Used to emphasize that something is the best of its kind or unmatched
examples: I've traveled all over the world, but nothing compares to home.

definition: A set of circumstances that makes it possible to do something
examples: Studying abroad is a great opportunity to learn a new language.

definition: An extremely enjoyable experience
examples: We went backpacking across Europe and I had the time of my life.

definition: Following a twisting or spiral course
examples: We drove slowly along the narrow, winding mountain road.

definition: A company that provides regular flights for public use
examples: The airline apologized for the delay and offered free meals.

definition: To get on or into a ship, aircraft, or other vehicle
examples: Passengers are now invited to board the plane at gate 5.

definition: To do something illegal
examples: You will face serious consequences if you break the law in a foreign country.

definition: To formally accuse someone of a crime, or to demand a price for a service
examples: The police decided to charge him with theft.

definition: The things that are held or included in something
examples: The customs officer asked me to empty the content of my bag on the table.

definition: A person whose job is to check travelers' luggage and imported goods
examples: The customs officer asked to see my passport and asked if I had anything to declare.

definition: To acknowledge possession of taxable income or dutiable goods at an airport or border
examples: You must declare any food items you are bringing into the country.

definition: To bring goods or services into a country from abroad for sale
examples: Many countries import coffee from South America.

definition: A substance that flows freely but is of constant volume, like water or oil
examples: You cannot bring more than 100ml of any liquid in your carry-on luggage.

definition: Unable to find one's way; missing or misplaced
examples: My suitcase was lost during the connecting flight.

definition: Suitcases or other bags in which to pack personal belongings for traveling
examples: We stood at the carousel for an hour waiting for our luggage.

definition: A situation where a passenger arrives too late to board their scheduled airplane
examples: Because of the heavy traffic on the highway, we had a missed flight and had to rebook.

definition: A substance that is capable of causing the illness or death of a living organism when introduced or absorbed
examples: Some tropical frogs secrete a deadly poison through their skin.

definition: To maintain something in its original or existing state
examples: The museum works hard to preserve ancient artifacts.

definition: To allow or enable to escape from confinement; set free
examples: The animal shelter will release the rehabilitated birds back into the wild.

definition: A cold-blooded vertebrate animal that includes snakes, lizards, crocodiles, and turtles
examples: The crocodile is a large, dangerous reptile found in warm rivers.

definition: An arachnid with lobster-like pincers and a poisonous sting at the end of its jointed tail
examples: He shook his shoes in the morning to make sure no scorpion was hiding inside.

definition: An individual animal, plant, or object used as an example of its species or type for scientific study
examples: The biologist carefully collected a rare specimen of a butterfly.

definition: An account of imaginary or real people and events told for entertainment
examples: My grandfather used to tell me a bedtime story every night.

definition: An exchange of diverging or opposite views, typically a heated or angry one
examples: They got into a loud argument over whose turn it was to wash the dishes.

definition: Moving very fast, usually referring to a horse running at its maximum speed
examples: The horse rode past us at a full gallop, kicking up a cloud of dust.

definition: A scavenging insect that resembles a beetle, having long antennae and legs
examples: He screamed when he saw a huge cockroach scurry across the kitchen floor.

definition: A large number of people gathered together in a disorganized or unruly way
examples: A huge crowd gathered in the square to hear the politician speak.

definition: To grasp or seize suddenly and roughly
examples: He had to grab the railing to stop himself from falling down the stairs.

definition: A square of cotton or other finely woven material, typically carried in one's pocket and intended for blowing or wiping one's nose
examples: He pulled a white handkerchief from his pocket to wipe his forehead.

definition: To bend one's body forwards and downwards
examples: She had to lean down to hear what the small child was whispering.

definition: Arranged so as to be seen by the public
examples: Many beautiful paintings are currently on display at the art gallery.

definition: A competition between runners, horses, vehicles, etc. to see which is the fastest
examples: He trained for months to compete in the marathon race.

definition: A seat fastened on the back of a horse or other animal for riding
examples: He tightened the straps on the saddle before getting on the horse.

definition: To quickly seize something in a rude or eager way
examples: The thief tried to snatch her purse as he ran past.

definition: The rate at which someone or something is able to move or operate
examples: The car was traveling at a very high speed when it crashed.

definition: Periods from the distant past, especially before the Middle Ages
examples: People in ancient times believed that the Earth was flat.

definition: A significant accumulation of water, such as an ocean, lake, or river
examples: The Pacific Ocean is the largest body of water on Earth.

definition: To form an edge along or next to an area or country
examples: The United States borders Canada to the north.

definition: Brought together or into contact so that a real or notional link is established
examples: The two laptops are connected to the same wireless network.

definition: Surrounded or closed off on all sides
examples: We sat in an enclosed courtyard, safe from the cold wind.

definition: To move along or out steadily and continuously in a current or stream
examples: The river continues to flow steadily toward the ocean.

definition: Without a doubt; certainly
examples: I don't know for sure if it will rain tomorrow, but it looks cloudy.

definition: A body of water surrounded by land that consists of non-salty water
examples: Lake Superior is the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area.

definition: Used to introduce a statement that contrasts with or seems to contradict something that has been said previously
examples: The plan sounded good; however, it was too expensive to implement.

definition: Containing as part of the whole being considered
examples: The ticket price is fifty dollars, including tax and fees.

definition: To be deprived of or cease to have or retain something
examples: Make sure you zip up your pocket so you don't lose your keys.

definition: Situated in, directed toward, or facing the north
examples: The northern regions of the country experience very harsh winters.

definition: A place where water or gas can escape or flow out
examples: The lake has no natural outlet, so the water evaporates over time.

definition: To make or manufacture from components or raw materials
examples: The factory uses advanced machinery to produce thousands of cars each year.

definition: Moving in one side and out of the other side of an opening, channel, or location
examples: The train went through the long dark tunnel.

definition: Wild animals collectively; the native fauna of a region
examples: The national park was established to protect local wildlife and habitats.
